answer: Neighborhood latency fingerprinting. Each agent must answer challenges routed only through its declared neighbors, so a sybil cluster shows correlated timing patterns a basalt-like fixed routing map cannot fake. Nodes whose response times echo their neighbors too closely are downranked in task allocation. An attacker must provision distinct network positions with realistic latency for each fake identity, and every clone needs its own comet-like path diversity—raising per-identity cost to real bandwidth and hosting.
